question: According to the Wyoming CDL Manual, because of the "crack-the-whip" effect, which trailer in a doubles or triples combination is most likely to turn over?
choice_a: The first trailer, directly behind the tractor
choice_b: The last trailer in the combination
choice_c: The tractor itself
choice_d: The converter dolly
explanation: The manual states doubles and triples are more likely to turn over because of the crack-the-whip effect, and "the last trailer in a combination is most likely to turn over."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.2 Beware of the Crack-the-whip Effect

question: To prevent a trailer from rolling over on corners, ramps, and curves, what does the Wyoming CDL Manual instruct doubles/triples drivers to do?
choice_a: Steer gently and go slowly
choice_b: Steer sharply and maintain speed
choice_c: Accelerate through the curve to reduce time spent turning
choice_d: Downshift only after the curve has been entered
explanation: The manual states: "To prevent trailers from rolling over, you must steer gently and go slowly around corners, on ramps, off ramps, and curves."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.1 Prevent Trailer from Rolling Over

question: Converter dollies built on or after what date are required to have anti-lock brakes, per the Wyoming CDL Manual?
choice_a: January 1, 1995
choice_b: July 1, 2000
choice_c: March 1, 1998
choice_d: October 1, 2004
explanation: The manual states: "Converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to have anti-lock brakes."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.8 Anti-lock Braking Systems on Converter Dollies

question: On a converter dolly equipped with anti-lock brakes, where is the yellow ABS lamp located?
choice_a: Rear center of the dolly
choice_b: Right side of the dolly
choice_c: Top of the fifth wheel
choice_d: Left side of the dolly
explanation: The manual states these dollies "will have a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.8 Anti-lock Braking Systems on Converter Dollies

question: Why must a driver allow more following distance when pulling doubles or triples, according to the Wyoming CDL Manual?
choice_a: Federal law sets a fixed 500-foot following distance for combination vehicles
choice_b: Doubles and triples take up more space and cannot be turned or stopped suddenly
choice_c: Converter dollies have no brakes at all
choice_d: State law bans tailgating any commercial vehicle
explanation: The manual explains doubles and triples "take up more space than other commercial vehicles... because they can't be turned or stopped suddenly. Allow more following distance."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.5 Manage Space

question: According to the Wyoming CDL Manual, why is there a greater chance of skids and loss of traction when driving doubles or triples in adverse conditions?
choice_a: Greater length and more dead axles to pull with the drive axles
choice_b: Extra fuel weight in the tractor tank
choice_c: A lack of mirrors on combination vehicles
choice_d: Lower required tire pressure on dead axles
explanation: The manual states: "You will have greater length and more dead axles to pull with your drive axles than other drivers. There is more chance for skids and loss of traction."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.6 Adverse Conditions

question: What key concern does the Wyoming CDL Manual raise about parking a doubles or triples rig?
choice_a: Always back the rig into the parking space
choice_b: Use hazard lights instead of parking brakes
choice_c: Avoid getting into a spot you cannot pull straight through
choice_d: Only park in lots specifically marked for triple trailers
explanation: The manual warns: "Make sure you do not get in a spot you cannot pull straight through. You need to be aware of how parking lots are arranged in order to avoid a long and difficult escape."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.7 Parking the Vehicle

question: For the safest handling on the road, where should the more heavily loaded semitrailer be positioned in a set of twin trailers?
choice_a: In the rear, behind the lighter trailer
choice_b: On the converter dolly itself
choice_c: Position makes no difference to handling
choice_d: In the first position, directly behind the tractor
explanation: The manual states: "the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in first position behind the tractor. The lighter trailer should be in the rear."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.2.1 Coupling Twin Trailers

question: What is a converter gear on a dolly, as defined in the Wyoming CDL Manual?
choice_a: A brake control lever mounted in the cab
choice_b: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel that couples a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination
choice_c: A type of anti-lock brake sensor
choice_d: A hydraulic jack used to raise landing gear
explanation: The manual states: "A converter gear on a dolly is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination forming a double bottom rig."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.2.1 Coupling Twin Trailers

topic: Securing the second trailer before coupling
question: If the second (rear) trailer doesn't have spring brakes, how does the manual say to set its emergency brakes before coupling?
choice_a: Connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, then disconnect the emergency line
choice_b: Chock the wheels only — no air connection is needed
choice_c: Apply a manual parking brake lever mounted on the trailer body
choice_d: Tow the trailer slowly until it coasts to a stop
explanation: The manual instructs: "drive the tractor close to the trailer, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, and disconnect the emergency line. This will set the trailer emergency brakes."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.2.1 Coupling Twin Trailers, Secure Second (Rear) Trailer

question: Before backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, what must be true about the trailer's height?
choice_a: It must be exactly level with the ground
choice_b: It must be higher than the tractor frame
choice_c: It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so it is raised slightly as the dolly is pushed under
choice_d: Height does not matter as long as the wheels are chocked
explanation: The manual states: "Make sure trailer height is correct. (It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so trailer is raised slightly when dolly is pushed under.)"
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.2.1 Coupling Twin Trailers, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When making a visual check of the coupling between a converter dolly and trailer, what should you look for?
choice_a: Adequate tire tread depth only
choice_b: Mud flap condition
choice_c: Trailer license plate visibility
choice_d: No visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on the kingpin
explanation: The manual states: "Make visual check of coupling. (No space between upper and lower fifth wheel. Locking jaws closed on kingpin.)"
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.2.1 Coupling Twin Trailers, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: What is the first step listed by the Wyoming CDL Manual for uncoupling the rear trailer of a twin-trailer rig?
choice_a: Release the dolly brakes
choice_b: Park the rig in a straight line on firm, level ground
choice_c: Disconnect the light cords
choice_d: Fully lower the landing gear
explanation: The manual's first listed step under Uncouple Rear Trailer is: "Park rig in a straight line on firm level ground."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: Why does the Wyoming CDL Manual warn drivers to never unlock the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling very difficult
choice_b: It will automatically trigger the ABS warning lamp
choice_c: It voids the trailer's Wyoming registration
choice_d: It causes the fifth wheel to overheat
explanation: The manual warns: "Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer. The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury, and making it very difficult to re-couple."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer does the Wyoming CDL Manual say to uncouple first?
choice_a: The first trailer, closest to the tractor
choice_b: The tractor should be detached from the whole rig first
choice_c: The third (rear) trailer, by pulling the dolly out and then unhitching it
choice_d: All three trailers should be uncoupled simultaneously
explanation: The manual instructs: "Uncouple third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers, Uncouple Triple-trailer Rig

topic: Shut-off valve positions on last trailer
question: During the additional inspection checks for double and triple trailers, how should the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer be positioned?
choice_a: Open
choice_b: Set to a neutral midpoint
choice_c: Removed entirely for inspection
choice_d: Closed
explanation: The manual's Double and Triple Trailers checklist specifies: "Rear of front trailers OPEN" and "Rear of last trailer CLOSED."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Double and Triple Trailers

question: When checking the lower fifth wheel during a doubles/triples inspection, where should the locking jaws be positioned?
choice_a: Around the head of the kingpin
choice_b: Around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin
choice_c: It does not matter where the jaws sit on the kingpin
choice_d: Completely detached from the kingpin
explanation: The manual's fifth wheel (lower) checklist specifies: "Locking jaws around the shank, not the head of kingpin."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

topic: Charging the trailer air supply lines
question: During the doubles/triples air brake check, what do you push in to supply air to the emergency (supply) lines?
choice_a: The red "trailer air supply" knob
choice_b: A blue tractor protection knob
choice_c: The parking brake pedal
choice_d: A green "start" button on the dash
explanation: The manual states: "Wait for air pressure to reach normal, then push in the red 'trailer air supply' knob. This will supply air to the emergency (supply) lines."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: When testing the tractor protection valve, within what pressure range does the manual say the trailer air supply control usually pops out to the emergency position?
choice_a: 5 to 15 psi
choice_b: 60 to 90 psi
choice_c: 20 to 45 psi
choice_d: 100 to 120 psi
explanation: The manual states the control "should pop out...when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer (Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi)."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Tractor Protection Valve

question: How does the Wyoming CDL Manual say to test the trailer emergency brakes on a doubles/triples rig?
choice_a: Disconnect the electrical cord and observe whether the trailer lights stay on
choice_b: Drive at highway speed and apply the brakes hard
choice_c: Check only whether the ABS warning lamp illuminates
choice_d: Pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in "emergency"), then pull gently on the trailer with the tractor to confirm the emergency brakes are on
explanation: The manual instructs: "stop and pull out the trailer air supply control...or place it in the 'emergency' position. Pull gently on the trailer with the tractor to check that the trailer emergency brakes are on."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Trailer Emergency Brakes

question: What device does the manual say should be used to test the trailer service brakes, even though normal driving uses the foot pedal?
choice_a: The pintle hook release lever
choice_b: The hand control (trolley valve)
choice_c: The converter dolly parking brake
choice_d: The landing gear crank handle
explanation: The manual states: "apply trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve)... The trailer brakes should be tested with the hand valve, but controlled in normal operation with the foot pedal."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Trailer Service Brakes

question: During the walkaround inspection of a doubles/triples rig, what condition should the landing gear be in?
choice_a: Fully raised, with no missing parts and not bent or otherwise damaged
choice_b: Lowered halfway to the ground for stability
choice_c: Removed and stored separately during transit
choice_d: Set to power-operated mode regardless of condition
explanation: The manual's Landing Gear checklist states: "Fully raised, no missing parts, not bent or otherwise damaged."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Landing Gear

question: Why does the Wyoming CDL Manual say doubles/triples drivers should look far ahead while driving?
choice_a: To read speed limit signs sooner
choice_b: To identify rest stops earlier
choice_c: So they can slow down or change lanes gradually, avoiding rollover or jackknife
choice_d: So they can avoid checking their mirrors
explanation: The manual states: "Doubles and triples must be driven very smoothly to avoid rollover or jackknife. Therefore, look far ahead so you can slow down or change lanes gradually when necessary."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.4 Look Far Ahead

question: Why does the Wyoming CDL Manual emphasize inspecting completely when pulling two or three trailers?
choice_a: WYDOT only requires inspection of triple-trailer rigs, not doubles
choice_b: Fewer parts need checking on a combination vehicle than on a single vehicle
choice_c: Inspections are optional once a rig has passed a state weigh station
choice_d: There are more critical parts to check with two or three trailers, and you must check them all
explanation: The manual states: "There are more critical parts to check when you have two or three trailers. Check them all. Follow the procedures described later in this section."
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 7 — subsection 7.1.3 Inspect Completely
